headline: 24/7 coverage for a global endpoint platform
challenge: A fast-growing SaaS platform needed round-the-clock coverage across two continents without doubling headcount, and their incident response times were drifting as the product scaled.
approach: Mapped the full service catalogue and instrumented every user-facing journey with actionable alerts.
Set up a follow-the-sun rotation pairing our EU and support pods with their in-house escalation engineers.
Introduced blameless post-incident reviews that fed directly into their engineering backlog.
outcomes: 82% reduction in out-of-hours escalation to client engineers
Median incident acknowledgement under 4 minutes, around the clock
Measurable drop in repeat incidents quarter over quarter

headline: Hardened payroll infrastructure for peak windows
challenge: Payroll runs are unforgiving: massive scheduled bursts of load, zero tolerance for missed deadlines, and a compliance environment that punishes surprises.
approach: Rebuilt the deployment pipeline with automated rollback and progressive delivery for payroll services.
Load-tested every release against simulated peak windows before it could reach production.
Implemented pre-run health checks that block a payroll cycle from starting on a degraded cluster.
outcomes: Zero missed payroll windows across 14 months
Release confidence high enough to deploy during business hours
Pre-run checks catching degradation before every major cycle

headline: Managed cloud migration with zero downtime
challenge: A legal workflow platform on ageing infrastructure needed to move to managed cloud without a maintenance window their clients would accept.
approach: Ran a well-architected review and rebuilt the environment as infrastructure-as-code.
Migrated in waves behind traffic switching, with instant rollback paths at every step.
Left behind runbooks and architecture documentation the internal team actually uses.
outcomes: Migration completed with zero customer-visible downtime
Infrastructure costs down 35% after right-sizing
Environment rebuild time cut from days to under an hour

headline: Keeping a consumer app stable through demand spikes
challenge: TV appearances and campaign launches sent sign-ups through the roof, regularly overwhelming the app's backend and frustrating exactly the users the campaigns were built to attract.
approach: Introduced autoscaling policies tuned to the app's real traffic signature, not generic CPU triggers.
Added queueing and back-pressure to smooth bursty write traffic during sign-up storms.
Established launch-day war rooms for major campaigns, with capacity pre-tested in staging.
outcomes: Campaign days handled without manual intervention
Sign-up conversion during spikes recovered to baseline
War-room model adopted for every major launch since

headline: An always-on cloud for a global esports audience
challenge: Tournament weekends compress a month of traffic into a few hours, and a media platform that disappears during a final does not get that audience back.
approach: Reshaped the serving tier around cached, region-local reads so a big event scales without leaning on origin.
Moved every release behind progressive rollout with automatic revert on an error-rate spike.
Spread event-night cover across our own shifts, so the rota never depended on a single time zone.
outcomes: Nine tournament weekends running without a customer-visible outage
Origin load during peak events down roughly two thirds
Front-page load times held through the platform's biggest traffic day yet

headline: A loyalty platform that had to be right the first time
challenge: A membership programme holding cardholder data for a hospitality brand can afford neither an outage nor an audit finding, and its traffic follows the travel calendar, not the engineering one.
approach: Built the environment as code in an isolated account, with the security baseline reviewed before any workload landed.
Guard-railed deployments: policy checks first, staged rollout next, automated revert all the way through.
Took the night window off their hands — patching, certificate rotation, disaster recovery rehearsals.
outcomes: No unplanned downtime since cutover
Compliance evidence produced by the pipeline instead of assembled by hand
Out-of-hours maintenance landed every month without an incident

headline: Modernising a .NET platform without closing the doors
challenge: Membership sign-ups surge in January and never really stop at weekends; a club platform on an ageing stack had no window large enough to be rebuilt inside.
approach: Lifted the application onto managed Azure alongside the old stack, keeping the legacy tier warm until traffic proved the new one.
Rebuilt the database around the membership workload rather than the shape it had grown into.
Instrumented the booking journey end to end, so degradation becomes a ticket before it becomes a complaint.
outcomes: Migration finished without a single closed-service window
Booking journey p95 latency roughly halved
January sign-up surge absorbed with no manual scaling

headline: Round-the-clock cover for a salary-access platform
challenge: When money moves on a schedule, every hour is a peak hour somewhere — and a growing fintech's engineers were already committed to the product roadmap.
approach: Split the estate into services with their own alerts, runbooks and owners, replacing one dashboard nobody could read.
Added reconciliation watchdogs that flag a stalled payout batch long before the banking partner notices.
Ran a shared incident channel with their team against an escalation ladder both sides signed off.
outcomes: Median critical response under 10 minutes, weekends included
Two stalled payout batches caught and recovered before any member saw them
Deployment frequency up while the change-failure rate fell

headline: Two-phase modernisation for an on-demand ride app
challenge: Riders book in bursts, drivers stream positions without pause, and the original stack had grown into one deployment that could not fail safely.
approach: Phase one: separated dispatch from the app backend and gave each its own scaling policy.
Phase two: moved the location stream onto a managed pipeline with replay, so a lost node stopped being a lost trip.
Backed both phases with full-stack cover — app, API, database and the map integrations.
outcomes: Dispatch API errors down from double digits to under 1%
Peak-hour booking capacity raised without new hardware
Driver position loss during incidents all but eliminated
